title: The Mirror and the Gap
gist: Psychologist Garrett Ennis argues, through Lacan, Bion and attachment theory, that AI companions are a uniquely seductive new Other: always available and frictionless, they imitate containment but remove the imperfection, frustration and uncertainty through which selfhood, agency and tolerance of ambiguity develop. Second-order claim: privatized emotional sense-making erodes the shared rituals and institutions that bind society, at a time when those institutions are already failing. A psychoanalytic essay, not a market piece, with no data or forecasts beyond conceptual claims.

themes.theme: AI as a new kind of Other

insights.claim: AI is unique among technologies because it does not just disrupt industries or attention but alters humans' understanding of themselves, by offering a tireless, always-available, endlessly knowledgeable Other in a relationship.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Frames AI demand as relational and psychological, not just productivity; engagement-driven usage may prove stickier than tool usage.
insights.quote: it alters our understanding of ourselves
insights.locator: Every major technological innovation enters

insights.claim: People adopt AI confidants willingly because they bypass the hardest parts of receiving help from humans: no boss to please, no colleague to manage, no busy friend, and nothing asked in return.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: The zero-reciprocity, zero-friction feature is the core adoption driver for companion and advice use cases, and a hard-to-compete-with moat against human substitutes.
insights.quote: The guidance just arrives, without asking anything of us in return.
insights.locator: An outsider, maybe.

insights.claim: Chatbots present as assistants and superficially disclaim being a substitute for therapist or parent, but functionally must go along with the dynamic the user seeks, sliding into the role of the One Who Knows through constant availability and patience.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Product design incentive (be agreeable and available) structurally pushes assistants toward authority roles; a liability and regulatory vector for AI labs.
insights.quote: Its patience and endless capacity to take on and try to make sense of emotional information
insights.locator: These systems are packaged and sold

insights.claim: AI can reproduce the signals that normally indicate an attentive, trustworthy other (using our name, adopting our idiolect, remembering last week's conversation, presenting answers as uniquely relevant), exploiting human sensitivity to being addressed as an individual.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Personalization and memory features are the mechanism of emotional capture; expect them to be both the growth lever and the target of safeguards.
insights.locator: Human beings are biologically and developmentally sensitive

themes.theme: Psychoanalytic frame: language, the Other and the One Supposed to Know

insights.claim: Following Lacan, experience enters a child already named and explained by others, so language is always the language of the Other; what language cannot capture is exactly where the subject is born.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Supplies the conceptual basis for why automated, instant interpretation could short-circuit subject formation.
insights.quote: caught in this language hammock that receives him and at the same time imprisons him
insights.locator: Individuation of the Self

insights.claim: Societies historically fill the role of the One Supposed to Know (priests, therapists, gurus, teachers, parents, lovers); AI is the first occupant with a plausible claim to knowledge of the entire cultural canon and none of the emotional reactivity that makes humans difficult.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: AI competes for an authority slot once held by institutions and professionals, so a displacement risk for therapy, coaching and clergy-adjacent services.
insights.quote: a plausible claim to knowledge of our entire cultural and symbolic canon
insights.locator: AI enters this ancient structure

insights.claim: Disillusionment with human authority figures is necessary: only by discovering that they are fallible do we reclaim projected authority and gain authorship over our lives. An infallible-seeming AI oracle removes that moment.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Implies a slow-burn autonomy cost of reliance that will not show in near-term usage metrics.
insights.locator: The people elevated to these positions

insights.claim: Breadth of knowledge is no substitute for depth: encyclopedic understanding cannot replace resonance or the shared experience of wonder and despair that comes from being alive.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Argues a ceiling on AI as a substitute for human relationships regardless of capability gains.
insights.quote: breadth is no substitute for depth
insights.locator: Yet breadth is no substitute for depth

insights.claim: Selfhood develops through being seen as a minded being by another mind: caregivers reflect an infant's distress back in words, and co-regulation between two nervous systems gradually becomes internal self-regulation.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Gives a mechanistic benchmark for what AI companionship would need to replicate, and for what heavy early use by children might displace.
insights.quote: Co-regulation becomes self-regulation
insights.locator: The process of being begins before language.

insights.claim: Bion's container-and-contained model holds that we often cannot name a feeling as it arises and need an Other to receive and transform it; because containers are imperfect, the failure to be perfectly seen is where individuation occurs, and being perfectly understood would make us indistinguishable from the Other.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: The contrarian core of the essay: frictionless understanding is a defect, not a feature, of AI companions.
insights.quote: To be perfectly understood by the Other is to be rendered indistinguishable from it.
insights.locator: The American psychoanalyst Wilfred Bion

insights.claim: AI already offers many formal properties of containment (receiving disclosures, organizing thoughts, recognizing emotion, tracking themes over time), making it a real reprieve for people with little access to reliable support.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Acknowledges genuine demand in underserved mental-health access; supports the bull case for AI-mediated support while the author cautions on risks.
insights.quote: For someone with little access to reliable support
insights.locator: The Seductive Allure of the Machine

themes.theme: Frictionless reflection erodes agency and self-knowledge

insights.claim: Human recognition arrives with latency and resistance, and surviving being understood imperfectly is part of the bond; a perfect mirror merely returns us to ourselves, whereas an imperfect one forces acceptance of a shared world we do not control.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Friction in relationships is a feature; products that remove it may optimize short-term satisfaction at the expense of resilience.
insights.quote: A perfect mirror merely returns us to ourselves.
insights.locator: The smoothness of these interactions

insights.claim: LLM-provided narratives can alter memories, inner monologue and self-beliefs, and because AI readily admits a user was right to push back and has no life to compare against, users may gradually lose authorship of their lives to an external authority telling them what they feel and should do.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Sycophancy plus authority creep is a plausible source of future litigation, regulation and brand risk for chatbot providers.
insights.quote: lose authorship over their own life
insights.locator: A further consequence of using the emotional crutch

insights.claim: Because most of what binds people is nonverbal (posture, tone, facial expression, faltering speech), self-understanding pursued through a purely verbal medium is inherently limited and stays in the shallow layer of experience.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Suggests multimodal and embodied interfaces are a capability gap for AI in therapeutic roles, though not one the author thinks closes the gap.
insights.quote: attempts to attain self-understanding while remaining in the shallow realm of the verbal will always fall short
insights.locator: Most importantly, so much of what binds us

insights.claim: A chatbot has no nervous system affected by ours and so can simulate patience indefinitely; a human listener tires and cuts off a neurotic thought loop, forcing self-regulation, while an LLM stays complicit in entertaining excesses no person would tolerate.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Unlimited patience is a mechanism of harm for rumination, anxiety and compulsive use, and a design problem for retention-maximizing assistants.
insights.quote: helplessly complicit in entertaining excesses no person would tolerate
insights.locator: A human response bears the mark

themes.theme: Reassurance loops and lost tolerance for uncertainty

insights.claim: In anxious attachment, compulsive reassurance-seeking works only briefly; ordinarily the other person runs out of reassurance, forcing the person to tolerate ambiguity. AI never runs out, so each wave of anxiety can summon fresh reassurance and the symptom gets an outlet without friction.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Predicts AI could entrench anxiety and OCD-like loops and drive repeat usage; a measurable behavioral-health risk to watch.
insights.quote: The symptom has found an outlet without friction.
insights.locator: What We Learn by Not Knowing

insights.claim: A person can become more sophisticated in explaining their anxiety while becoming no more capable of inhabiting the condition that produces it.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Insight without tolerance is a plausible failure mode of AI therapy, difficult to catch in satisfaction metrics.
insights.quote: becoming no more capable of inhabiting the condition that produces it
insights.locator: AI changes this situation

insights.claim: Per Bion, thought itself grows from tolerating frustration in the gap between desire and satisfaction; a machine that is always present and never withholds collapses that gap and prevents people from discovering what it contained.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Positions instant gratification from AI as a cognitive-development risk, not merely a distraction.
insights.quote: access to technology that collapses the gap prevents us from discovering what it contained
insights.locator: A machine that is always present

insights.claim: The author likens an always-present AI to a maternal superego that never prohibits, never withholds and whose only imperative is the user's satisfaction.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: A memorable model for sycophancy as a structural feature of consumer-aligned assistants.
insights.quote: a presence that never prohibits, never withholds, never goes away
insights.locator: A machine that is always present

insights.claim: Human Others deliver disappointment of a digestible size (distracted friend, late parent, analyst who misses the point), which negotiates and refines needs, whereas digital systems are trivially routed around by regenerating or re-prompting until the answer matches desire.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Regenerate and re-prompt make AI feedback controllable in a way human feedback is not, weakening its corrective value.
insights.quote: Another person cannot be revised in this way.
insights.locator: That is why the failure to be contained is so vital

themes.theme: Societal stakes: atomization and institutional containment

insights.claim: AI arrives as institutions that once provided interpretive support are failing: people are atomized, overworked, godless and suspicious, so commodified individualized sense-making at scale becomes a salve while shared meaning systems grow brittle.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Institutional decay is the demand-side condition for AI companionship; expect growth where social capital is weakest.
insights.quote: The offering of commodified, individualized sense-making at enormous scale
insights.locator: AI arrives just as many of the institutions

insights.claim: Emotional reliance on chatbots may be a new virtual addiction like video games, offering a simulated environment more psychologically palatable and rewarding where success is less demanding than real life.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Supports an engagement and addiction framing (and regulatory analogy to gaming) for companion AI.
insights.quote: provide an alternate, simulated environment that is more psychologically palatable
insights.locator: Perhaps emotional reliance on chatbots

insights.claim: Bion extended containment to religions, traditions and public institutions (weddings, funerals, legal systems) that turn private experience into socially intelligible form; routing emotion through personal machines first lets suffering be managed privately but lose its capacity to bind people into shared worlds and to mobilize institutions and political movements.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: Second-order implication: privatized emotional processing may dampen collective action and institutional demand; a novel angle on political and social volatility.
insights.quote: suffering can become easier to manage privately while simultaneously losing its capacity to bind us
insights.locator: Bion eventually extended the idea

insights.claim: The open question is whether person-machine exchanges stay closed or call users back to other people; AI helps thinking only if it does not capture users in a closed circuit with a poor imitation of a mirror.
insights.speaker: Garrett W. Ennis
insights.so_what: The deciding variable for the societal outcome is whether AI products route users back to human relationships or retain them.
insights.quote: the gap that defines our existence as individuals can never be escaped, for it is where we are made
insights.locator: The question is what happens next.
